gap: No result ChatGPT got (of those I could read) states that the only 16-inch 2560x1600 120 Hz UPERFECT panel a named reviewer put a colorimeter on measured 238 nits against 400 advertised (Parkablogs), that the ASUS ZenScreen MB16QHG measured 479 to 481 nits against its 500 claim (Tech Advisor, MonitorNerds), and that no instrument measurement turned up for any other in-line screen I searched, the Duex Float 2 Pro included.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's best portable monitors for Mac (read in full, updated 2026-11-25) and PCWorld's roundup (read in full, updated 2026-06-26). Macworld lists the Duex Float 2 Pro at 'up to 350' nits and 100% sRGB without saying they were measured, and has no UPERFECT 16-inch, SOTSU or ASUS MB16QHG. PCWorld gives 337 nits for the Arzopa Z1FC and 457 nits for the ViewSonic VX1655-4K-OLED, and has no 16-inch 16:10 120 Hz screen. Two cited rivals could not be fully checked: the RTINGS page returned only navigation, and TechRadar's page was cut off after its first pick (MSI Pro MP165 E6), with the Arzopa Z3FC visible only in a photo caption. If RTINGS's body carries measured brightness for a 16:10 120 Hz panel, this drops to 1.
decides: It does not name a winner; it tells the page how much weight the brightness column can bear. Ranking the line on listed nits is unsafe: the one measured UPERFECT 16-inch 2560x1600 panel reached 59.5% of its advertised figure, so the GR16EQ's 450 cd/m2 and the 400 to 470 nit Amazon listings should be labelled maker claims and should not win on brightness alone. The only in-line screen with measured brightness near its claim is the ASUS MB16QHG, which the desk notes say is out of stock at ASUS (I did not re-read that). The Duex Float 2 Pro's 350 nits is also a claim, so it holds its segment on being the stacked layout, not on a measured figure. I read no store prices or stock for this angle.
candidates: UPERFECT GR16DQ (formerly UGame C2 / UPlays C2)
Arzopa Z1RC (60 Hz, outside the line)

findings.label: Measured maximum brightness against advertised
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Parkablogs, Teoh Yi Chie, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: Colorimeter not named. 238 / 400 = 59.5% of the claim. The review gives 0.72 kg and 12 W rated power, the same as the desk notes' GR16DQ store page (which now says 350 cd/m2), so this is probably the same panel family as the GR16DQ and Amazon B0BHNLZCNF; that match is my inference, not stated by any source. The unit is from 2023 and current stock may differ. It is not a measurement of the 144 Hz GR16EQ.

findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Parkablogs, Teoh Yi Chie, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: Parkablogs measured these after calibration; no Delta E or contrast was reported.

findings.label: Power and macOS notes from the reviewer

findings.note: Instrument not named. 479 / 500 claimed = 95.8%. Price at review $399. The review says HDR 'approaches 500 nits'.

findings.value: 481 cd/m2; 1504:1 at 50% brightness; 100% sRGB, 98% DCI-P3, 86% Adobe RGB; average dE 3.12 out of the box, 0.96 calibrated
findings.source_title: ASUS ZenScreen MB16QHG Review (MonitorNerds, Paolo Reva, 2023-08-04)
findings.note: Colorimeter not named. 481 / 500 claimed = 96.2%. Weight 2.65 lb is from the spec list, not weighed. The page's spec list says 144 Hz while its text says 120 Hz.

findings.product: Arzopa Z1RC (16-inch 2560x1600, 60 Hz, outside the line)
